blocks.text: The young boys are pressed to convert, threatened, and mocked with promises of ease if they abandon the path of their house, but their answer is defiance rather than fear. (26–29)
The violence becomes physical and public, and the scene is narrated as one of cruelty without pity, leading to the killing of the younger Sahibzadas before a watching world. (30–32)
The page leaves no ambiguity: the younger Sahibzadas are martyrs, and the atrocity is framed as something that should have torn both sky and earth apart. (33)
